anna-ops: Quick q — runbook says get approval before copying logs off-host. If I'm triaging a P1 and need to copy a small snippet to my laptop for debugging, is that allowed? Also what's the fastest approval flow?

sophia-sec: Short answer: no copying full logs to personal machines. Allowed paths:
- use secure-scratch (ephemeral host)
- export only redacted snippets
- request `prod-debug` access in the portal (session will be recorded)

Runbook excerpt:
```
Prod debug access: request via https://redwood.internal/requests
Include: ticket id, justification, approver (@oncall-manager)
Session must be recorded; exports go to secure-scratch only.
```

oncall-bot: +1 Please file an access request: https://redwood.internal/requests/new — include the `prod-debug` tag and the approver's handle. Sessions auto-recorded. :white_check_mark:

matt-eng: If you need a quick redaction, use this pipeline on the host and then scp to secure-scratch:
```
sudo journalctl -u my-service | rg -v "(auth_token|kv_cache)" | sed -E "s/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/[REDACTED_EMAIL]/g"
```
Don't `scp` to your laptop. Also avoid copying full request bodies or KV caches.

julio-dev: Are screenshots allowed if I blur creds? Sometimes it's faster to screenshot a single error line.

sophia-sec: Screenshots are allowed only when all PII/keys are redacted. Prefer text redaction for auditability. Minimal checklist:
- record ticket id in the session
- redact emails, ips, tokens
- never export KV caches or raw request payloads
- keep exports on secure-scratch for <30d

anna-ops: Got it — I'll file the request and use secure-scratch. Thanks all :pray:
